newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Hoiupank makes latest Estonian move into Latvia.
newsitem.headline: Hoiupank makes latest Estonian move into Latvia.

text.p: Hoiupank on Monday became the latest Estonian bank to move into the share market of neighbouring Latvia, as it bought 76 percent of a local broker.

Hoiupank joins what is an onslaught of Estonian financial institutions into Latvia and Lithuania. Estonia's largest bank Hansapank has bought a bank in Latvia and Tallinna Pank has set up a pan-Baltic investments subsidiary.

Hoiupank said it bought the majority of Inveks, which was launched in 1995 and has share capital of 45,240 lats ($79,600). It said that Inveks had 10 percent of the Latvian securities market and was mainly active on the over-the-counter market.

"We plan to channel the whole of Hoiupank's security business through Inveks and start analysis (of Latvian companies) on the spot," Heino Viik, the head of Hoiupank's markets department, told Reuters.
Viik would not say how much Hoiu paid for its 76 percent stake in Inveks nor give any profit or turnover forecasts.
Hoiupank's strategy includes an expansion of its securities activities into Lithuania but there were no concrete talks at the moment, Viik added.
Inveks said it would continue with its plans to boost its activity on the market.
"We plan to work more intensively with the new controlling stake owner in place," Jevgeny Bogdanov, executive manager of Inveks, told Reuters.
"Inveks will become a member of the cental depository next week, at the latest during this month, and then buy shares in the bourse," Bogdanov said.
"Inveks could be considered as one of the leaders of the free market and we ended last year with a profit," he added.
